newsitem.title: INDIA: INDIAN CINEMA -- Latest weekly box office.
newsitem.headline: INDIAN CINEMA -- Latest weekly box office.

text.p: INDIAN FILM BOX OFFICE REPORT FOR WEEK TO OCT 23, 1996
JEWEL THIEF STRIKES BACK AHEAD OF GENERALLY DULL DIWALI FARE

Pre-Diwali holiday weeks are generally dull in the movie theatre and this year proved no exception. Added to box-office woes was the one-week postal and telecom strike nationwide, making it difficult to tabulate various centres. Only the major urban cities were able to report, giving some indication of the current week's box-office trend.

RETURN OF THE JEWEL THIEF, a sequel to JEWEL THIEF, was released this week, trying to re-capture the sparkle of the 27-year-old hit suspense comedy. Some of the original players like Dev Anand, Ashok Kumar, Prem Chopra and Dharmendra revived roles along with newer stars like Jackie Shroff and Sadashiv Amrapurkar joining in the jewel heist fun.

Although the super hit directed by Vijay Anand might not compare with Ashok Tyagi's new take on the subject, it was number one at the box-office and might be able to attract viewers of both generations.

RAJA KI AAYEGI BAARAT (The King's Wedding Procession will Come) introduces Ranee and Shadaab Khanee as lead stars and is showing signs of a surprise hit due to its interesting story line. The film narrates the tale of a raped girl, who feels she has no future in India for marriage, asks for justice in court to marry her rapist.
To save himself from jail, he consents to this request and proceeds to humiliate and harm her in the marriage. But the girl's endurance ultimately wins over her husband.

Although the film fared badly on opening day, the word of mouth about the good dialogue and story-line brought box-office collection up by 95 percent daily. Similiar to BANDIT QUEEN, the story of rape seems to have onece more struck a titilating accord with the audience. Distributors should expect some good profits from the film.

ZORDAAR could not survive in the box-office and DILJALE is proving that it still has appeal. HINDUSTANI is keeping steady and perhaps as India's Oscar nomination in the Foreign Film category, it might be able to play outside India.

Foreign films, though few, are doing well. THE ROCK especially has been well-received in the south and MISSION IMPOSSIBLE in the English version is drawing good crowds in Bombay. CASINO's drop in collections in Bombay proved that it was a gamble to have this three-hour film screened in India.

Late-night (10:30 p.m.) screenings of English films seem to be doing well and attracting the right young crowds. Films like THE USUAL SUSPECTS and THE AMERICAN PRESIDENT seem made for late-night viewing.
